_evidence: Key-frame stream at esi for 0x0040abc1, which parses records with 0x40aadb until a zero header (CF=1 exit at 0x40ac12) and runs [0x62ac44] = header & 0x7ff steps per record ('sub dword [0x62ac44],1; je 0x40abf7' then the next record; a zero count with a nonzero header starts the counter at 0 and loops 2^32 times: the 8/10 timeouts of stream_0040aadb, whose headers allow count 0 and 0x7ff). A record is header + (0x8000: 2 words) + cx + start (+1 word with 0x4000) + (0x2000: end, +1 word with 0x4000), 6..16 bytes, so record boundaries move with the flags: every word of the 64-byte stream is therefore drawn from one list that is 0 (about 30%: the terminating header, or zero data) or a valid header with count 1..0x15 and the flag bits 0x8000/0x4000/0x2000/0x1000/0x800 in many combinations. Whichever offset the next header lands on, it is a terminator or a record with a small nonzero count (idiv by the count never sees 0), and the zero guard memory after the buffer ends any longer chain, so the walk ends after a few records and at most ~10*0x15 steps. Data words (start/end/cx/+2/+4) take the same small and sign-bit patterns.
